newsitem.title: MEXICO: Rebel leader, Mexican left demand peace in Chiapas.
newsitem.headline: Rebel leader, Mexican left demand peace in Chiapas.

text.p: A masked Zapatista rebel leader made a rare appearance here on Tuesday rallying Mexican students in demand of renewed peace talks in the southeastern state of Chiapas.

"Keep your word, Mr. President," read banners displayed throughout a plaza at Mexico City's main university, where protesters flocked to see Commander Ramona, one of the most charismatic figures of the Zapatista movement.

The protesters accused President Ernesto Zedillo of reneging on a partial peace agreement on Indian rights that government negotiators signed with the Zapatista National Liberation Army (EZLN) a year ago.

Based on that accord, all-party Congressional mediators drew up proposals to change the constitution to promote Indian rights. But the government rejected the draft bill, saying it would grant Indians autonomy and fragment the country.

Commander Ramona, who first came to Mexico City in September for a kidney transplant, received a hero's welcome upon arriving at the rally. Wearing a ski mask and traditional dress, she gave a 20-minute speech in the Tzotzil language.
"We are going to win and we are going to construct a Mexico with all of you," Ramona said in her few words of Spanish at the end of the speech.
The Zapatistas, predominantly Maya Indians, launched an armed rebellion in Chiapas on Jan. 1, 1994, and about 145 people died in two weeks of fighting.
Peace talks that began in 1995 broke down last year, and have shown little sign of getting back on track with both sides accusing each other of negotiating in bad faith.
